items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: But I did think of, in the church of Papa John, once in Japan, I said to Papa John Joseph, who at 89 ought to know, I said, Papa John, you ought to know, where did jazz come from?

ctx.x: What did you, what, uh, can you describe the service?

Uh, again I got the feeling of a ritualistic dance or chant rather than a service. I listened to the minister, uh, he started reading text, it didn't really make much sense, it didn't have much continuity, just as pure English. It didn't have much to do with George Lewis. And then his reading gradually began to take on rhythmic overtones, and it became a chant. And you felt that if it were only kept up a little longer, the whole audience would let go. It was, it was a catharsis. It was an emotional experience.…
He said, from the Baptist church. Yes.
